content: In the United States, only 50.5% of adults with diabetes successfully maintain an A1C level below 7%, and a mere 22.2% are able to control all three critical risk factors simultaneously. Specific groups, including young adults, racial and ethnic minorities, and individuals with limited English proficiency, encounter additional obstacles that hinder effective diabetes management. The economic burden of diabetes in the United States is substantial, amounting to approximately $413 billion annually. This figure encompasses both direct healthcare costs and losses in productivity, underscoring the urgent need for enhanced and better-coordinated approaches to diabetes care.
